# Configuration reference

> Typed config loader.
>
> Reads `.toml` from the package root (copy an example from config/) and validates it with pydantic so a malformed config fails at synth rather than at deploy.

Every key the CDK app reads, from the pydantic models in [packages/infra/config/loader.py](../../packages/infra/config/loader.py) and the comments above their fields. Templates: [config/dev.toml](../../packages/infra/config/dev.toml), [config/prod.toml](../../packages/infra/config/prod.toml). Unknown keys fail validation. Sections are in alphabetical order; keys keep the order of loader.py. Defaults and allowed values are TOML literals.

## `[api]`

Optional.

The ECS FastAPI service that fronts the Runtime for the web client.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allowIpList` | array of IP networks (CIDR) | `[]` |  | Who may reach the load balancer, besides the VPC. In Prod each entry must be /8 or longer (IPv6: /32) unless allowPublicIngress is set. |
| `allowPublicIngress` | boolean | `false` |  | Prod only: set true to accept allowIpList entries broader than /8 (IPv6: /32), such as 0.0.0.0/0, which open the load balancer to the internet. WAF still fronts it. |
| `serverPort` | integer | `8000` |  |  |
| `certificateArn` | string | `""` |  |  |
| `corsAllowOrigins` | array of strings | `["http://localhost:4000"]` |  |  |
| `minTasks` | integer | `1` | >= 1 |  |
| `maxTasks` | integer | `3` | >= 1 |  |
| `requestTimeout` | integer | `120` | 10 to 120 | Seconds one turn may take, end to end. At most 120: the load balancer's idle timeout is 150 s and the browser gives up after 130 s. |
| `wafRateLimit` | integer | `100` | 10 to 2000000000 | Requests one client IP may send in any 5 minutes before WAF blocks it. Shoppers behind one NAT share an IP, so raise it for offices and campuses; the WafRateLimitBlocks alarm reports blocks. |

## `[auth]`

Optional.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `provider` | string | `"cognito"` | `"cognito"`, `"oidc"` |  |
| `issuer` | string | `""` |  |  |
| `clientId` | string | `""` |  |  |
| `audiences` | array of strings | `[]` |  |  |
| `allowedClients` | array of strings | `[]` |  |  |
| `scopes` | array of strings | `["aria/chat"]` |  |  |
| `tenantClaim` | string | `""` |  |  |
| `callbackUrls` | array of strings | `["http://localhost:4000/auth/callback"]` |  |  |
| `logoutUrls` | array of strings | `["http://localhost:4000/"]` |  |  |
| `domainPrefix` | string | `""` | matches `^([a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?)?$` | Managed Cognito only: the prefix of the sign-in domain, &lt;prefix>.auth.&lt;region>.amazoncognito.com. Empty uses "&lt;namespace>-&lt;account ID>". Set it to keep the account ID out of the public login URL, before the first deploy: a pool has one prefix domain and CloudFormation creates the new domain before deleting the old one, so changing it later fails the update. The web app finds the domain through the issuer's discovery document. |
| `mfa` | string | `"optional"` | `"off"`, `"optional"`, `"required"` | Managed Cognito only: multi-factor sign-in for shoppers with an authenticator app (TOTP). "optional": a shopper who has registered an authenticator is asked for a code; managed login offers no enrolment, and the web app has no enrolment screen. Cognito advises it with threat protection. "required": managed login makes every shopper register an authenticator, and asks for a code at every sign-in. "off": no MFA. A deployed pool can switch between them. |

Checks in [loader.py](../../packages/infra/config/loader.py), as the errors they raise:

- `AuthConfig.validate_oidc`: BYO OIDC requires HTTPS issuer, clientId, and audiences or allowedClients
- `AuthConfig.validate_oidc`: At least one API access scope is required
- `AuthConfig.validate_oidc`: auth.domainPrefix can't contain aws, amazon or cognito; Cognito reserves them
- `AuthConfig.validate_oidc`: auth.mfa applies to managed Cognito only; with provider = oidc, MFA is your IdP's setting

`builtinEvaluators` is the customer-facing knob: add or remove built-in evaluator IDs (`aws bedrock-agentcore-control list-evaluators --region <region>` lists them all). Custom (domain-specific) evaluators are declared in components/evaluators.py and picked up automatically.

Optional.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | string | `"managed"` | `"managed"`, `"external"`, `"disabled"` | managed: provision the Gateway + targets here. external: point at an existing Gateway. disabled: no Gateway — the agent runs with no MCP tools. |
| `endpoint` | string | `""` |  |  |
| `allowedTools` | array of strings | `[]` |  |  |
| `authorizationVerified` | boolean | `false` |  |  |
| `targets` | array of tables: [`[[gateway.targets]]`](#gatewaytargets) | `[]` |  |  |
| `forwardHeaders` | array of strings | `[]` |  | Custom request headers to propagate end to end (client -> Runtime -> agent -> Gateway -> target). Non-credential context only, e.g. x-tenant-id, x-locale. Never credentials: the shopper's token never leaves the agent (docs/design-docs/identity-and-tokens.md). Never an x-aria-\* name, in any casing: that namespace is the agent's own. |
| `savedItemsSample` | boolean | `false` |  | A sample Lambda target that needs the shopper's identity (packages/mcp-servers/saved-items-lambda). It exercises the whole Gateway path: agent token, actor header, interceptor, target. |
| `agentAuth` | table: [`[gateway.agentAuth]`](#gatewayagentauth) | defaults below |  |  |

Checks in [loader.py](../../packages/infra/config/loader.py), as the errors they raise:

- `GatewayConfig.validate_forward_headers`: Do not propagate Authorization via forwardHeaders. The shopper's token never leaves the agent, and each Gateway target authenticates with its own credentials; see docs/design-docs/identity-and-tokens.md
- `GatewayConfig.validate_forward_headers`: gateway.forwardHeaders can't name {name}: the interceptor sets it from the calling trace, so targets can find the agent's trace
- `GatewayConfig.validate_forward_headers`: gateway.forwardHeaders can't name {name}: x-aria-\* headers are the agent's own, x-aria-actor-id among them, and forwarding one would let the shopper set it for local tools

### `[gateway.agentAuth]`

Optional.

How the agent authenticates to the Gateway. The shopper's JWT is never forwarded.

- `on_behalf_of`: AgentCore Identity exchanges the shopper's token (RFC 8693, delegation) for a Gateway token whose `sub` is the shopper and `act.sub` the agent.
- `m2m`: a client-credentials token for the agent's client. It doesn't name the shopper, so targets rely on the x-aria-actor-id header alone.

Managed Cognito creates the client and credential provider. A BYO IdP or an external Gateway names its own AgentCore Identity provider and scopes here.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `flow` | string | `"on_behalf_of"` | `"on_behalf_of"`, `"m2m"` |  |
| `credentialProvider` | string | `""` |  |  |
| `clientId` | string | `""` |  | BYO IdP only: the agent's own client. Required with a managed Gateway in both flows: the m2m authorizer and the interceptor accept only tokens issued to it. Never a shopper client. |
| `audience` | string | `""` |  | BYO IdP, on_behalf_of: the audience the Gateway token is minted for and the authorizer accepts. Never one of auth.audiences, which the shopper's own tokens carry. |
| `scopes` | array of strings | `[]` |  |  |

### `[[gateway.targets]]`

An array of tables: repeat the header once per entry.

A customer tool behind the Gateway. See docs/guides/gateway-onboarding.md for each kind.

- `lambda`: a Lambda function with an inline tool schema, called with the Gateway's IAM role.
- `mcp`: a remote MCP server, called with an OAuth or API-key credential provider.
- `openapi`: an HTTPS API described by an OpenAPI document (a JSON file in this repo, or S3). Each operationId becomes a tool; called with an OAuth or API-key credential provider.
- `apigateway`: a REST API stage. `operations` names the tools; called with the Gateway's IAM role (SigV4, execute-api:Invoke on that stage only) or an API key.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | required | matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,50}$` |  |
| `kind` | string | required | `"lambda"`, `"mcp"`, `"openapi"`, `"apigateway"` |  |
| `endpoint` | string | `""` |  |  |
| `lambdaArn` | string | `""` |  |  |
| `toolSchema` | array of tables | `[]` |  |  |
| `schemaFile` | string | `""` |  | openapi: exactly one of these. A file path is relative to packages/infra. |
| `schemaS3Uri` | string | `""` |  |  |
| `restApiId` | string | `""` |  | apigateway |
| `stage` | string | `""` |  |  |
| `operations` | array of tables: [`[[gateway.targets.operations]]`](#gatewaytargetsoperations) | `[]` |  |  |
| `allowedTools` | array of strings | required | at least 1 entry |  |
| `policyFile` | string | `""` |  | A Cedar template (.cedar) under components/policies/, relative to packages/infra, deployed once per allowed tool. Any folder there except sample/, which holds the saved-items sample's own policies. |
| `credentialType` | string | `"GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE"` | `"GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE"`, `"OAUTH"`, `"API_KEY"` |  |
| `providerArn` | string | `""` |  |  |
| `scopes` | array of strings | `[]` |  |  |
| `grantType` | string | `"CLIENT_CREDENTIALS"` | `"CLIENT_CREDENTIALS"` | OAUTH targets: the Gateway gets a token for your API's own client, and x-aria-actor-id names the shopper. |
| `apiKeyLocation` | string | `"HEADER"` | `"HEADER"`, `"QUERY_PARAMETER"` | API_KEY targets: where the Gateway puts the key, e.g. HEADER "x-api-key". |
| `apiKeyName` | string | `""` |  |  |

Checks in [loader.py](../../packages/infra/config/loader.py), as the errors they raise:

- `ToolTargetConfig.validate_grant_type`: grantType AUTHORIZATION_CODE needs a consent flow in the shopper's browser and a return URL, and ARIA has neither; use CLIENT_CREDENTIALS, the default, and identify the shopper by the x-aria-actor-id header
- `ToolTargetConfig.validate_target`: allowedTools must appear in the Lambda toolSchema
- `ToolTargetConfig.validate_target`: Lambda targets require lambdaArn, toolSchema and GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE
- `ToolTargetConfig.validate_target`: MCP targets require HTTPS endpoint and OAuth/API key providerArn
- `ToolTargetConfig.validate_target`: OpenAPI targets need exactly one of schemaFile or schemaS3Uri
- `ToolTargetConfig.validate_target`: schemaS3Uri must be an s3:// URI
- `ToolTargetConfig.validate_target`: OpenAPI targets need an OAuth or API key providerArn; use kind=apigateway for IAM-signed API Gateway calls
- `ToolTargetConfig.validate_target`: allowedTools must be operationIds in {schema_file}: {sorted(operation_ids)}
- `ToolTargetConfig.validate_target`: API Gateway targets need restApiId, stage and operations
- `ToolTargetConfig.validate_target`: API Gateway targets use GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE or API_KEY
- `ToolTargetConfig.validate_target`: API_KEY targets need providerArn
- `ToolTargetConfig.validate_target`: allowedTools must be operation names
- `ToolTargetConfig.validate_target`: API_KEY targets need apiKeyName, the header or query parameter that carries the key
- `ToolTargetConfig.policy_document`: policyFile must be a .cedar file under components/policies/, outside sample/: {policy_file}
- `ToolTargetConfig.policy_document`: policyFile {policy_file} does not exist under packages/infra
- `ToolTargetConfig.openapi_document`: schemaFile must be a .json file under packages/infra

## `[guardrail]`

Optional.

Bedrock Guardrail applied to the agent's model invocations.

AUDIT evaluates the content filters and reports matches in the trace without blocking; ENFORCE blocks. Disabling removes the guardrail entirely and is forbidden in prod, which also requires ENFORCE. streamProcessing is the stage's choice.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` |  |  |
| `mode` | string | `"ENFORCE"` | `"AUDIT"`, `"ENFORCE"` |  |
| `streamProcessing` | string | `"sync"` | `"sync"`, `"async"` | How replies stream through the guardrail. "sync" checks each reply before any of it reaches the shopper. On Dev, with the guardrail checking the whole conversation (Converse's default), "sync" reached first text about 0.9 s later than "async" (2.61 s vs 1.71 s; 0.76 s with no guardrail); checking only the latest message, as the agent does, "async" took 1.56 s. "async" streams at once and checks in the background: a reply that breaks a filter can show briefly before the stream is cut, and sensitive-information masking is unsupported. The shipped filters block rather than mask. |
| `screenToolResults` | boolean | `true` |  | Also check what Gateway tools return with the guardrail (ApplyGuardrail, as input) before the model reads it, against prompt injection planted in tool data. Local search results come from the configured catalog and aren't screened. A result the guardrail blocks, or can't check, reaches the model as an error. Has no effect when the guardrail is disabled. |

## `[memory]`

Optional.

AgentCore Memory settings.

Short-term memory, the store of conversation events, is always on: it is how a conversation survives a Runtime session that idled out, and what the session list and history read. `longTerm` turns extraction on: the strategies below distil events into preferences, facts and summaries retrieved into later turns. Off by default, since it keeps derived data about each shopper.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `longTerm` | boolean | `false` |  |  |
| `strategies` | table: [`[memory.strategies]`](#memorystrategies) | defaults below |  |  |
| `eventExpiryDays` | integer | `90` | 7 to 365 | Days AgentCore Memory keeps conversation events; the service accepts 7 to 365. |
| `topK` | integer | `5` |  |  |
| `relevanceScore` | float | `0.3` |  |  |

### `[memory.strategies]`

Optional.

Long-term extraction strategies, each an independent pipeline.

Only consulted when `memory.longTerm` is on; each maps to one CfnMemory strategy and one retrieval namespace in the agent. Toggling them updates the Memory resource in place, so the conversation history is kept.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `semantic` | boolean | `true` |  | user_facts — semantic facts about the shopper. |
| `summarization` | boolean | `true` |  | conversation_summaries — per-session recap for a returning conversation. |
| `userPreference` | boolean | `true` |  | user_preferences — cross-session sizes, colours, styles, brands. |

## `[policy]`

Optional.

AgentCore Policy (Cedar) settings for Gateway tool authorization.

Cedar is default-deny, so an incorrect policy set in ENFORCE mode removes the agent's tools entirely. Roll out in LOG_ONLY, read the decision logs, then switch.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `false` |  |  |
| `mode` | string | `"LOG_ONLY"` | `"LOG_ONLY"`, `"ENFORCE"` | LOG_ONLY evaluates and logs without blocking; ENFORCE actually denies. |

### `[tools.productSearch]`

Optional.

The agent's local search tool and the catalog behind it.

The catalog definition (`catalogFile`) names the catalog's fields, filters, search fields, embedded text and card mapping; the search tool, the index and the indexing job come from it. It is validated at load, so a bad definition fails synth.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `provider` | string | `"fixture"` | `"fixture"`, `"opensearch"`, `"http"`, `"disabled"` | fixture is the packaged example catalog, synthetic products searched in memory; Prod rejects it. |
| `endpoint` | string | `""` |  |  |
| `secretArn` | string | `""` |  |  |
| `openSearchIndex` | string | `"products"` | matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$` | The OpenSearch alias searched. Each load is a versioned index, &lt;alias>-&lt;version>. |
| `resultPath` | string | `"products"` |  |  |
| `catalogFile` | string | `""` |  | The catalog definition, a TOML file, relative to this config file. Empty for the packaged example (aria_catalog/example/catalog.toml), which the fixture provider always uses. |

Checks in [loader.py](../../packages/infra/config/loader.py), as the errors they raise:

- `ProductSearchConfig.validate_catalog`: tools.productSearch.catalogFile must be empty with provider = fixture: the fixture is the packaged example catalog, and searches it with the example's definition
- `ProductSearchConfig.validate_catalog`: tools.productSearch.catalogFile {path} must be an existing .toml catalog definition
- `ProductSearchConfig.validate_catalog`: tools.productSearch.catalogFile {path} is not a valid catalog definition: {error}

## Cross-section checks

`Config` validates the whole file after the sections. The errors it raises ([loader.py](../../packages/infra/config/loader.py)):

- Gateway target names must be unique
- {target.schema_file} declares {declared} as parameters. Remove them: the Gateway propagates these headers, and a declared parameter becomes a tool argument the model sets
- maxTasks must be >= minTasks
- gateway.savedItemsSample needs a managed Gateway
- Gateway tools with a BYO IdP or external Gateway need gateway.agentAuth.credentialProvider and scopes
- Gateway tools with a BYO IdP need gateway.agentAuth.clientId, the agent's own client; the Gateway interceptor accepts only tokens issued to it
- gateway.agentAuth.flow=on_behalf_of with a BYO IdP needs the audience
- gateway.agentAuth.audience must not be one of auth.audiences: the shopper's own tokens carry those audiences and would pass the Gateway's audience check
- gateway.agentAuth.clientId must not be a shopper client (auth.clientId or auth.allowedClients): the Gateway would accept the shopper's own tokens
- policy.mode=ENFORCE needs a policyFile for every customer target, missing for {missing}: Cedar denies by default, so those targets would lose every tool
- External gateway requires HTTPS endpoint and allowedTools
- gateway.endpoint must be an AgentCore Gateway URL, https://&lt;id>.gateway.bedrock-agentcore.&lt;region>.amazonaws.com/mcp
- External gateway cannot provision targets
- Cedar Policy runs on the Gateway; set policy.enabled=false when gateway is disabled
- Disabled gateway cannot host tool targets
- HTTP search requires an HTTPS endpoint
- memory.longTerm requires at least one strategy; set longTerm=false for short-term only
- Evaluations require verified Transaction Search, traceLogGroup, and explicit captureContent consent
- Prod managed VPC requires one NAT gateway per AZ
- Prod requires explicit app.account and app.region
- Prod requires certificateArn, allowIpList and minTasks >= 2
- Prod allowIpList entries {api.broad_ingress} are broader than /8 (IPv6: /32) and open the load balancer to the internet; set api.allowPublicIngress = true if that is intended
- Prod requires explicit HTTPS CORS origins
- Prod requires HTTPS OIDC callbacks and logout URLs
- Prod managed gateway requires Cedar ENFORCE
- Prod external gateway requires verified authorization
- Prod can't deploy gateway.savedItemsSample, a demo target that serves fixture data
- Prod can't deploy tools.productSearch.provider = fixture, the committed sample catalog; use http or opensearch for your own catalog, or disabled
- Prod requires alarmTopicArn
- Prod requires the guardrail enabled
- Prod requires guardrail.mode = ENFORCE: AUDIT blocks nothing, so try AUDIT on Dev
